 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Troy Aikman's future in ESPN's Monday Night Football booth has been a running storyline for much of the season. On Thursday morning, he made a comment on Dallas radio about his longtime partner, Joe Buck, and fans are now asking whether he will still be on the call when ESPN broadcasts its first Super Bowl in February.
 The remark came two days after ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro spoke publicly about the situation for the first time. Aikman and Buck, who form the longest-running booth pairing in NFL history, have kept calling games every week despite the reported tension.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Buck signed a six-year extension with ESPN in September, according to The Athletic, while Aikman has not signed a new deal. Front Office Sports reported in October that the two argued before a Monday Night Football game.
 Troy Aikman's Radio Comment About Joe Buck Draws Quick Reaction
 George Dunham was running The Musers by himself on "96.7 The Ticket" in Dallas when Aikman made his weekly appearance. Asked by Dunham about filling in on the show, the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback turned the question toward his broadcast partner.
 "Joe's always wanted a one-man booth. I'm wondering if you've always wanted a one-man radio show," Aikman said.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement When the talk turned to Buck presenting at the Country Music Awards on Wednesday night, Aikman kept his reply short: "Everywhere. Ubiquitous."
 Fans quickly started asking what the exchange could mean for Aikman's place in the Super Bowl booth.
 "I think the percentage chance of Aikman not doing the Super Bowl went from 5% to 20% with this comment. Magnus and Pitaro need to intervene in a more assertive way," one fan wrote .
 Another fan replied to that estimate with a much higher number: "I think it went to 100% and there's a good chance he's done now."
 A third fan skipped the percentages and made a flat prediction: "Aikman won't get to Super Bowl LXI."

 Another fan did not expect Aikman to last even another week in the booth: "He won't be back next Monday. They'll have to put Kelce or Riddick or whatever up there."
 Fans Ask Whether ESPN Keeps Aikman Through Super Bowl 61
 Other fans turned their attention to ESPN, with the Super Bowl now less than three months away.
 "Troy from the Top Rope. The question is now does ESPN pull him before the Super Bowl. Big storyline," one fan wrote .
 Another fan put the question to the network more bluntly: "Saying stuff like this ESPN CAN'T platform Aikman with SB-level viewership to just cross their fingers and hope he plays nice… can they?"
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Another fan went further: "No hate for Aikman and thoroughly enjoying watching this play out. With that said, ESPN would be nuts to keep him around. Dude is disgruntled with nothing to lose. Would give him a bag to let him walk and promote someone."
 That view runs against what Pitaro said two days before Aikman's latest comment. Pitaro spoke Tuesday at Sports Business Journal's Media Innovators conference.

 He said: "Are we happy about the media coverage recently? Of course not. It's been disappointing. But these guys are professionals and are delivering every week. I fully expect that to continue through the season and through the Super Bowl."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Buck and Aikman are also among several high-profile ESPN personalities not scheduled to attend the network's Super Bowl 61 media day on Dec. 1, although ESPN still lists both on its Super Bowl broadcast team.
